nodes.name: Cedar of Lebanon
nodes.desc: The reserve's signature conifer, forming forests on the slopes of Mount Barouk. Goat browsing on young trees hinders its natural regeneration.

nodes.name: Oaks
nodes.desc: Oak woodland, including kermes oak, is among the most recorded vegetation near the reserve. Acorns feed wild boar.

nodes.name: Syrian juniper
nodes.desc: A juniper of the mountain slopes that grows alongside cedar in Lebanon and Turkey.

nodes.name: Wild grasses
nodes.desc: Wild goatgrasses and other annual herbs of open slopes and clearings, grazed by wild and domestic hoofed animals.

nodes.name: Wild boar
nodes.desc: Omnivore that digs for roots and bulbs and eats acorns. Wolves are its main predator across much of its range.

nodes.name: Mountain gazelle
nodes.desc: A small gazelle listed among the reserve's mammals and a recorded prey of red fox.

nodes.name: Nubian ibex
nodes.desc: Extinct in Lebanon since the mid-19th century; a herd from Jordan was brought to the reserve in 2017. It eats grasses and leaves and stays near cliffs for safety.

nodes.name: Cape hyrax
nodes.desc: A rock-dwelling herbivore recorded near the reserve.

nodes.name: Domestic goat
nodes.desc: Browsing by goats on young cedars hinders regeneration of the forest. Jackals and wolves take livestock.

nodes.name: House mouse
nodes.desc: Small omnivorous rodent eaten by jackals, foxes, hedgehogs and snakes in recorded GloBI interactions.

nodes.name: Golden jackal
nodes.desc: Opportunistic omnivore that eats rodents, birds, reptiles and fruit, and scavenges carcasses. Wolves dominate it.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Generalist hunter and scavenger; GloBI records it eating gazelle, mice, hedgehogs and snakes among these species.

nodes.name: Southern white-breasted hedgehog
nodes.desc: Small ground forager; GloBI records it eating mice and snakes.

nodes.name: Large whip snake
nodes.desc: A fast, large snake; GloBI records it eating mice. Hunted by jackals, foxes and snake eagles.

nodes.name: Short-toed snake eagle
nodes.desc: Eats mostly snakes, plus some lizards. Populations in the Middle East are resident.

nodes.name: Griffon vulture
nodes.desc: Raptor listed among the reserve's birds. It feeds on carcasses of large animals.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: Listed among the reserve's mammals. Wolves are the main predator of wild boar and dominate jackals.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: A large eagle listed among the reserve's raptors; it is a recorded predator of Nubian ibex.

nodes.name: Winter snow
nodes.desc: Heavy snow cover blankets the high cedar slopes and melts into water for spring growth.

nodes.name: Winter rain
nodes.desc: Mediterranean winter rains water the oaks and grasses.

nodes.name: Limestone soil nutrients
nodes.desc: Nutrients in the reserve's limestone soils, returned by decomposers.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and invertebrates recycling dead wood, leaves and carcasses.
